summary: Trusted verification failed (exit 2); candidate retained as WIP for repair. V3-07 candidate adds a coherent new Research Analytics Plane module (src/analytics: types, taxonomy, classification cache, privacy transform pipeline, release gate, differential privacy, query budget, consent policy, buyer contracts, audit log) plus a 1151-line test suite. Trusted verification FAILED with exit code 2 (8 TypeScript errors, all in the new test file) — a mandatory mustFix, so the decision cannot be accept. Independent re-runs confirm: npx tsc --noEmit reproduces the same 8 errors; npx jest on the candidate suite gives 60 passed / 10 failed; all 18 previously accepted suites (380 tests, V3-01..V3-06) still pass, so no regression. Five must-fix findings remain: (1) trusted verification exit 2 — test-file type errors at lines 434, 501-505, 730, 870; (2) fundamental pipeline contradiction — validateNoOperationalIds lists 'label' as a forbidden input field while transformContributionCreated/transformEntryCreated REQUIRE label for classification, so every contribution and V2-entry fact is rejected at stage 1 ('Operational/free-text field label detected') and the contribution/entry transform paths are dead code, breaking the core acceptance 'événements V3 couvrent contributions dépenses settlements usage'; (3) the gate tests 'approves clean product with proper provenance' and 'audit log entry is generated' can never pass — assessReIdentificationRisk flags any dataset < 10 records with re_identification_risk (high), which blocks approval (5-record and empty datasets both rejected); (4) query budget test expects remainingQueriesThisMinute=1 but the service returns 2 (limit 3 - 0 used - 1); (5) consent expiry test is a same-millisecond race — retentionDays:0 with strict '<' comparison makes a just-created record not expired when recordConsent and getExpiredRecords run in the same millisecond (fails in jest, passes standalone). Non-blocking observations: the new module is not wired to the existing ResearchAnalyticsGateway port / LocalResearchAnalyticsAdapter (still a no-op) and the 'asynchrone/incrémentale/checkpointée' pipeline aspects are represented only by a passive checkpoint data structure with no cursor driver or async scheduler; types.ts header claims 'ZERO operational IDs' while ConsentRecord.userId and PipelineCheckpoint.householdId are operational IDs (defensible as operational-side records, but the header invariant is overstated); the gate computes requiresDifferentialPrivacy but never enforces it in approval; PipelineCheckpoint.id uses Date.now()+Math.random() (non-deterministic). The delta is coherent and mostly functional (taxonomy, cache, DP, query budget, consent, buyer contracts, audit log, gate all work; 60/70 candidate tests pass) — repair, not reject.

findings.problem: Trusted product verification failed with exit code 2: 8 TypeScript errors in __tests__/domain/v3-07-analytics-privacy.test.ts. Lines 501-505 pass partial records { taxonomyCategoryId, month, beneficiaryCount } missing required union fields (type, unit, value, hasPersistentTask, wasPlanned, timestamp). Line 730 passes 'commercial-use' which is not a DataProcessingPurpose. Line 870 casts AnonymousAnalyticsEvent directly to Record<string, unknown> (needs 'as unknown as').

findings.requiredFix: Fix the test file types: cast intentionally-malformed records with 'as unknown as' or 'as any' where the test deliberately injects forbidden fields (line 434, 870); use full valid event shapes or casts for the clean-product records (lines 501-505); replace 'commercial-use' with a valid DataProcessingPurpose (e.g. 'synthetic-data-generation') or cast the argument (line 730). Then rerun the full trusted gate.

findings.path: src/analytics/pipeline.ts (validateNoOperationalIds lines 131-151 vs transformContributionCreated lines 252-292 / transformEntryCreated lines 205-247)
findings.problem: Fundamental pipeline contradiction: validateNoOperationalIds lists 'label' (and 'title', 'notes') as forbidden input fields, but transformContributionCreated and transformEntryCreated REQUIRE a label for classification. Every contribution_created and entry_created fact is therefore rejected at stage 1 with 'Operational/free-text field label detected in input data' before the transform functions are reached. The contribution and V2-entry transform paths are dead code, breaking the core V3-07 acceptance 'événements V3 couvrent contributions dépenses settlements usage' and the constitution's classification-ready raw operational data requirement (label must be consumed for classification but never emitted).
findings.evidence: Independent npx jest: 'rejects entry with free text in forbidden fields' receives 'Operational/free-text field label detected in input data' instead of the expected 'notes'; 'transforms contribution_created correctly', 'transforms V2 entry_created (backward compatible)', 'batch transform handles mixed valid and invalid facts', 'pipeline input (OperationalFact) never reaches output', and 'V3 events cover contributions, expenses, settlements, usage' all fail with result.success=false for labeled facts. Code inspection confirms 'label' is in forbiddenFields (line 137) and required at lines 221-226 and 268-270.
findings.requiredFix: Allow label as pipeline INPUT (it is consumed for classification and never emitted): remove 'label'/'title'/'notes' from the input-forbidden list (or restrict input validation to operational IDs only) and rely on the output event types + PrivacyReleaseGate to guarantee no free text in outputs. Add a test proving a labeled contribution fact transforms successfully AND the emitted AnonymousContributionEvent contains no label/title/notes field.
findings.verification: All contribution/entry pipeline tests pass: labeled contribution_created and entry_created facts transform with success=true; emitted events contain no free-text fields; the free-text rejection test still rejects a fact carrying notes.

findings.path: __tests__/domain/v3-07-analytics-privacy.test.ts (lines 492-520 'approves clean product with proper provenance'; lines 531-555 'audit log entry is generated')
findings.problem: The two gate tests expecting approved=true can never pass with the current gate logic. assessReIdentificationRisk flags any dataset with fewer than minCohortSize*2 (10) records with re_identification_risk (high severity), and high violations block approval. The clean-product test uses 5 records (also triggering reconstruction_risk and 4 rare_cell violations) and the audit-log test uses empty data — both are rejected (approved=false), so the tests fail at runtime even after the typecheck errors are fixed.
findings.evidence: Independent execution of PrivacyReleaseGate.validate on the exact test data: 'approves clean product' → approved=false, violations [rare_cell x4 (medium), reconstruction_risk (medium), re_identification_risk (high)], riskScore 0.7; 'audit log entry is generated' (data: []) → re_identification_risk (high) → approved=false. Jest confirms both tests fail with Expected true / Received false.
findings.requiredFix: Make the test data satisfy the gate's own anti-reconstruction rules: use >= 10 records with repeated (category, month, beneficiaryCount) combinations so combinations.size <= facts.length * 0.8 and facts.length >= minCohortSize*2, and use non-empty data for the audit-log test (or assert the gate's actual conservative behavior instead of approval). Do not weaken the gate's re-identification protections.
findings.verification: Both tests pass with approved=true while the gate's anti-reconstruction checks remain intact (a genuinely small/unique dataset is still rejected).

findings.problem: Test/implementation mismatch: 'allows queries within budget' expects remainingQueriesThisMinute=1 after the first query with rateLimitPerMinute=3, but QueryBudgetService.checkBudget returns rateLimitPerMinute - queriesThisMinute - 1 = 3 - 0 - 1 = 2 (two queries remain after this one). The test fails at runtime.
findings.evidence: Independent npx jest: 'allows queries within budget' fails — Expected: 1, Received: 2. Code inspection: queryBudget.ts line 92 computes remainingQueriesThisMinute as limit - queriesThisMinute - 1.
findings.requiredFix: Align test and implementation: either assert 2 (queries remaining after this query) in the test, or change the service to report remaining-including-current (limit - queriesThisMinute - 1 is the 'after this query' count; if the intended semantics is 'remaining including this one', return limit - queriesThisMinute). Pick one documented semantic and make the test match it.
findings.verification: The query-budget test passes and the reported remaining count matches the documented semantics.

findings.problem: Flaky consent-expiry test: retentionDays:0 makes cutoff = Date.now() and getExpiredRecords uses a strict '<' comparison (new Date(r.timestamp).getTime() < cutoff). When recordConsent and getExpiredRecords execute within the same millisecond (as in jest), the record timestamp equals the cutoff and the record is NOT expired — the test fails with expired=0. Standalone execution with a 1ms gap passes, proving the race.
findings.evidence: Independent npx jest: 'expired consent records can be purged' fails — Expected >= 1, Received 0. Standalone execution of the same consentPolicy.ts code path returns expired=1 (record ts ...065, cutoff ...066).
findings.requiredFix: Make the test deterministic: use a negative retentionDays (e.g. -1) so cutoff is strictly in the future of any just-created record, or change getExpiredRecords to '<=' so a zero-retention record created in the same millisecond is expired, or inject a clock. Keep the retention semantics documented and deterministic.
findings.verification: The consent-expiry test passes reliably across repeated runs (no same-millisecond race).

findings.requiredFix: Resolve the concrete failing trusted check without discarding already-correct candidate work, then rerun the full gate.
